acceptance.requirement: semanticGraph and runtimeProjection use independent schemas, validators, digests and persisted files; neither object accepts fields owned by the other layer.
scopeDigest, semanticGraphInputDigest and runtimeProjectionDigest cover only their declared facts and remain canonical under irrelevant ordering.
Completion comment, completed close and declared delivery-label changes are reconciled against one sealed expected mutation registry and classified projection-only.
Ready, blocked, slot, lease, epoch, candidate, delivery, cleanup, telemetry and resource changes update runtimeProjection only and never dispatch a DAG updater.
Unexpected dependency, owner, conflict, contract or acceptance-group changes select semantic-patch and authorize exactly one fresh read-only DAG updater.
Ordinary semantic updates accept only minimal base-bound patches with allowed operations, direct evidence digests, a recomputable result digest and no embedded full graph.
Full proposals are limited to initial-create, graph-corruption-recovery and explicit scope-replacement, with machine-bound recovery evidence and reason.

The deterministic projector consumes immutable ledger plus semantic graph, does not reinterpret or edit semantic edges/classes, and recomputes completed prerequisites, ready/blocked nodes, critical path, conflicts, leases, slots and frontier.

#1832 DAG update decision receipts bind all before/after layer digests, expected-mutation reconciliation, patch/full identities, updater dispatch identity and projector identity with mode-specific nullability.
#1826 counters are derived from verified decision receipts and falsePositiveDagDispatchCount is exactly zero.
Root may register remote side effects and accept an unchanged updater output, but cannot author, edit or apply a graph patch; projector has no patch authority.

One shared semantic/runtime contract has no compatibility fallback: one initial full graph, event append plus projection replay after completion, patch-only ordinary updates and full recovery only for bounded reasons.
